# @lidtop/opencode-gh-pr-status

Never leave a review waiting. See the GitHub pull requests that need you in the sidebar, with your pull requests, your reviews, and your teams' review requests one command away.

[![Watch the GH PR Status demo: pull requests waiting on you in the sidebar, the /ghpr tabs, and review comments sent to the agent](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZackarySantana/opcode/main/docs/images/gh-pr-status-demo.jpg)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8ccd999c-d742-4e8a-ac69-7ed7096f4fed)

*The 55-second demo uses sample pull requests and a scripted agent reply.*

## Install

Requires OpenCode **2.2.0 or newer in the 2.x line**, and the [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com/) signed in with `gh auth login` where the OpenCode server runs.

```sh
opencode plugin add @lidtop/opencode-gh-pr-status
```

Or add it to `plugins` in your global `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` (or `opencode.json`), keeping your existing entries:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": ["@lidtop/opencode-gh-pr-status"]
}
```

**Where it runs.** The server side runs `gh`, refreshes on the schedule, and keeps your settings; the sidebar and `/ghpr` in the terminal show what it has, over plugin RPC (both parts use the ID `opcode-gh-pr-status`). Configure it where the server reads plugins (this config, or the remote server's), not in `cli.json`: a terminal-only install has no server side to ask, and the sidebar and `/ghpr` say to add it to the server's plugins. `gh` must be installed and signed in where the OpenCode server runs, which is a remote machine when you connect to one.

**One source of truth.** Every terminal connected to the same server shows the same pull requests and settings. The server polls GitHub once for all of them, however many terminals or projects are open, and a change to a setting or the team filter, or a refresh, shows in every terminal right away.

## Use

Run `/ghpr` or select **Pull requests** in the command palette. The dialog has five tabs:

- **Mine:** your open pull requests. The ones that need you come first, then the ones waiting on others, then drafts.
- **Reviewing:** pull requests requesting your review by name, then open ones you've already reviewed. Requests only for your teams are on Teams.
- **Teams:** review requests for your teams, with every requested reviewer listed. Press `f` to show one team; the choice is saved until you pick **All your teams** there.
- **Orgs:** which orgs' pull requests show. See [Orgs](#orgs).
- **Settings:** the order of pull requests, which inactive ones to leave out, what the sidebar shows, and how often it refreshes.

Each pull request shows its status, author, repository and number, when it came to you, and who is requested and when: you first, then your teams, then everyone else. It came to you when your review, or your team's, was requested; for your own, when a reviewer first commented or requested changes; otherwise when it opened.

The **Order** setting sorts each group, and the sidebar, by that time:

- **Smart** (the default) puts pull requests that need your eyes first: review requests for you by name, and your own pull requests where a reviewer commented or requested changes and you haven't requested their review again since. The rest follow. Both parts are oldest first.
- **Newest** and **Oldest** sort by time alone.

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `tab` / `shift+tab` | Next / previous tab |
| `↑` / `↓`, `j` / `k` | Move the outline |
| `/` | Search titles, authors, repositories, statuses, and reviewers (orgs on Orgs) |
| `enter`, `space` | Open the outlined pull request in your browser (clicking one does too); choose the outlined org (Orgs) |
| `f` | Show one team's review requests, or all of them (Teams) |
| `←` / `→`, `h` / `l` | Change the outlined setting (Settings); switch between Exclude and Include (Orgs) |
| `r` | Refresh now |
| `esc` | Leave the box, clear the search, close the team picker, then close |

A pull request **waits on you** when:

- it requests your review, or your team's, and you haven't reviewed it since (GitHub can keep a team's request after you review, such as one a ruleset requires);
- it's yours and has merge conflicts, failing checks, or a reviewer's comments or requested changes, or is approved and ready to merge.

Statuses are colored by urgency: red for your pull requests that are blocked, yellow for review requests (**Review requested** for you, **Team: web** for your team), green for approved, the theme's highlight for pull requests waiting on someone else, and gray for drafts and pull requests you've approved or commented on.

The sidebar lists review requests waiting on you, your teams' (narrowed to the team chosen on the Teams tab), and all your open pull requests, as one list in the **Order** setting's order. Each shows how long ago it came to you. It lists five by default, then a count of the rest and a pointer to `/ghpr`; with nothing to list it's just the title. Beside the title, a countdown shows the time to the next refresh. Click a pull request there to open it in your browser, or the "+N more" line to open `/ghpr`.

Links open in your browser with `open` (macOS), `rundll32` (Windows), or `xdg-open` (Linux); on WSL it tries `wslview`, `xdg-open`, then PowerShell.

### Desktop

In OpenCode Desktop, a pill above a session's composer counts the pull requests waiting on you, colored by the most urgent. Its menu lists them as the sidebar does (following the sidebar settings, team filter, and **Sidebar items**, then "N more in Pull requests", which opens the full list); pick one to open it in your browser. When pull requests can't be read, the pill turns red and its first row says why; pick it to refresh.

Select **Pull requests** in the command palette, or run `/ghpr`, to search every pull request, grouped as the terminal's tabs group them, and open one. **Refresh pull requests** refreshes now. Settings, the team filter, and the orgs shown are changed in a terminal; the desktop app follows them. The desktop app asks the app's own server, at the routed session's location or the server's default on Home.

## Teams and hidden pull requests

Review requests come from GitHub's `review-requested:@me` search, which includes requests to any team you're on, closed and secret teams included, as long as `gh` can see them. Team names come from `gh api /user/teams`, which needs the `read:org` scope that `gh auth login` grants by default; without it, every team requested on a pull request that asks for your review is treated as yours.

GitHub sometimes withholds results. A pull request in an organization that enforces SAML single sign-on stays hidden until you authorize `gh`'s token for that organization, and a team your token can't see shows as **hidden team**. `/ghpr` counts what was withheld and says what to do, such as authorizing GitHub CLI for an organization's single sign-on at [github.com/settings/connections/applications](https://github.com/settings/connections/applications).

## Orgs

The **Orgs** tab narrows every tab, the sidebar, and the desktop pill and list by the org that owns each pull request's repository (a user, for personal repositories). It lists every org that owns a repository with an open pull request in the last refresh, plus the orgs of your teams and any you chose before, each with how many pull requests the lists show for it.

- Press `enter` or `space`, or click, to choose an org or unchoose it. Press `/` to search them; `enter` in the box chooses the outlined match, so you can choose several in a row.
- In **Exclude** mode (the default) the chosen orgs' pull requests are hidden; in **Include** mode only theirs show. `←` / `→` switches the mode and keeps what you chose. With nothing chosen, everything shows in either mode.

The other tabs say how many pull requests the Orgs tab hides. The choices are saved with the settings, and each change applies to what's saved, so changes made at once in different terminals all stick.

Only what GitHub's searches return is listed, up to 50 pull requests per list, and the searches aren't narrowed: a hidden org's pull requests still count toward that limit.

## Settings

| Setting | Choices | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Order | Smart, Newest, Oldest | Smart |
| Ignore inactive | Off, 7 days, 14 days, 1 month, 3 months, 1 year | 1 month |
| Sidebar team reviews | No, Yes | Yes |
| Sidebar own PRs | No, Yes | Yes |
| Sidebar items | 3, 5, 10, 15, 20 | 5 |
| Refresh every | 1m, 2m, 5m, 10m, 15m, 30m | 5m |

**Ignore inactive** leaves a pull request out of every tab and the sidebar once it has gone that long without activity on GitHub, such as a push, comment, review, or review request, however long ago it opened. Off lists them all.

Review requests for you always appear in the sidebar. **Sidebar team reviews** adds your teams' review requests, narrowed to the Teams tab's filter; **Sidebar own PRs** adds your pull requests that need you. Each refresh runs one GraphQL search per list, up to 50 open pull requests each, once for every terminal on the server. The server keeps refreshing while it has the plugin loaded, even with no terminal open.

Settings and the team filter are saved in the server's plugin storage and shared by every terminal connected to it. If the server can't read them, it shows the defaults and refuses changes until it can, so your saved settings are never replaced. Settings saved by versions before the server kept them aren't carried over: they start at the defaults.

## Data and privacy

The server's plugin storage keeps your settings and team filter. Pull requests are kept in the server's memory only, and sent to the terminals connected to it. Requests go to GitHub through `gh` on the server, with its credentials. Nothing else is sent.

Earlier versions kept settings in `opcode-gh-pr-status/gh-pr-status.sqlite` in the terminal's OpenCode state directory (`$XDG_STATE_HOME/opencode`, or `~/.local/state/opencode`). Nothing reads it now, so you can delete it.

## Development

From the repository root:

```sh
mise exec -- bun test plugins/gh-pr-status/test
mise exec -- bun run typecheck
mise run dev gh-pr-status
```

The build bundles the private `@opcode/core`, `@opcode/tabs`, and `@opcode/ui` workspaces into the package; OpenCode, OpenTUI, and Solid stay external.

# @lidtop/opencode-gh-pr-status

## 0.5.0

### Minor Changes

- 2540a17: `/ghpr` has an **Orgs** tab, before Settings, to choose which orgs' pull requests show, everywhere: exclude the chosen orgs, or include only theirs. It lists every org with an open pull request, and your teams' orgs, with counts, to choose from and search. The other tabs say how many pull requests it hides.

### Patch Changes

- b4b8592: Bundles the updated shared core, which adds the side-session metadata tag that Review and Cost use. No change in behavior.
- 1394e9e: Remove `/ghpr-comments` (**Send PR review comments**) from the terminal and the desktop app, along with its `commentsPrompt` server option.
- 9c2b277: The shared card list every plugin bundles can show a pane beside the list, which Snippets uses for its preview. Nothing changes for this plugin.

## 0.4.0

### Minor Changes

- 4fe433a: Add a refresh button at the right end of the sidebar section's title line, beside the countdown to the next refresh.

## 0.3.0

### Minor Changes

- e44fa40: Add an OpenCode Desktop part: a pill above the composer listing the pull requests waiting on you (open one in the browser, or refresh when they can't be read), **Pull requests** (`/ghpr`) to search every pull request grouped as the terminal's tabs, **Refresh pull requests**, and **Send PR review comments** (`/ghpr-comments`), which puts the review comments into the session's composer for you to review and send.
- 62c9603: Require OpenCode 2.2.0 and OpenTUI 0.7.

## 0.2.3

### Patch Changes

- 915e7ff: A new **Ignore inactive** setting (Off, 7 days, 14 days, 1 month, 3 months, 1 year) leaves a pull request out of `/ghpr` and the sidebar once it has gone that long without activity on GitHub, such as a push, comment, review, or review request. It defaults to 1 month.
- 5ccffe8: GH PR Status now runs on the OpenCode server, so every terminal connected to it shows the same pull requests and settings, and GitHub is polled once for all of them instead of once per terminal. A change to a setting or the Teams tab's filter, or a refresh with `r`, shows in every terminal right away, and the sidebar's countdown follows the server's schedule. Configure the plugin where the server reads plugins (`opencode.json(c)`, not `cli.json`), with `gh` installed and signed in on the server's machine; without the server side, the sidebar and `/ghpr` say to add it; `/ghpr-comments` reads the session's branch there too. `commentsPrompt` is now a server option, and the `database` option is gone: settings live in the server's plugin storage. If the server can't read the saved settings, it shows the defaults and refuses changes until it can, rather than overwrite them. Settings saved by earlier versions are not carried over and start at the defaults; you can delete `opcode-gh-pr-status/gh-pr-status.sqlite` in the terminal's OpenCode state directory.
- e91635a: Shared code that Feed and GH PR Status use moved into helpers every plugin bundles: the minute clock that ages views, and sending changes to the server in order while showing them at once. Nothing changes for any plugin.

## 0.2.2

### Patch Changes

- 31ba0af: Pull requests are ordered by when they came to you, not GitHub's last update, and a new **Order** setting (Smart, Newest, Oldest) chooses how. Smart, the default, puts pull requests that need your eyes first: review requests for you by name, and your own pull requests where a reviewer commented or requested changes and you haven't requested their review again since. The rest follow, both parts oldest first. The sidebar is one list in that order and now includes all your open pull requests. Each pull request shows the time it sorts by: when your review, or your team's, was requested; when a reviewer first asked for changes to yours; otherwise when it opened. A reviewer's comments on your pull request now mark it **Review comments**, and requested changes clear once you request that reviewer again. Settings saved by earlier versions can't be read: delete `opcode-gh-pr-status/gh-pr-status.sqlite` in OpenCode's state directory before upgrading.

## 0.2.1

### Patch Changes

- e5df44d: The README opens with a short demo video.

## 0.2.0

### Minor Changes

- dabd5c5: Add `/ghpr-comments`, which sends the open review feedback on the current branch's open pull request to the open session as your prompt, asking the agent to verify each comment and come back with an action for it. Resolved threads, bots, and your own threads, reviews, and comments are left out; outdated threads stay, marked with the line they were on. The `commentsPrompt` option replaces the instructions.

### Patch Changes

- e9e45a3: The sidebar no longer warns about review requests GitHub withheld; `/ghpr` still counts them and says what to do.
- bb097fd: Require OpenCode 2.1.3 or newer.
- 3c06421: Stop listing a review request as waiting on you once you've reviewed since it was made. A team request that GitHub keeps after your review (such as one a ruleset requires), or a request GitHub's search still lists after you approved, no longer appears in the sidebar; a request made again after your review still does. Your latest review is now read with `viewerLatestReview`, since `latestReviews` can leave it out.
- 1708674: Move Later's prompt paste helper into the shared UI package so Snippets can reuse it. No behavior changes.
- c1cfd3c: Clicking "+N more in /ghpr" or "+N more in /feed" in the sidebar now opens the dialog and keeps it open. Before, the dialog closed again as soon as the mouse button was released.
- 44bad65: The Pull requests and Feeds sidebar sections show their refresh countdown beside the title instead of on a line of their own. Those sections and Agents no longer add a line saying there's nothing to show; they show just the title.
- e85fab8: The shared tabbed dialog can keep its open tab when shown again, for Later. No behavior changes.
- f27f920: The shared item card can lead with its title when an item has no head, for Later. No behavior changes.

## 0.1.0

### Minor Changes

- 86148b3: Add GH PR Status: the GitHub pull requests waiting on you, in the sidebar, from the GitHub CLI. `/ghpr` lists your pull requests, the ones you review, and your teams' review requests with every requested reviewer, a saved team filter, and when each was opened and your review requested. Click or press `enter` to open one in your browser.
